---
title: "AI-Assisted Federal Survey Harmonization"
subtitle: "Cross-Survey Integration Analysis of 47 Census Bureau Demographic Surveys"
date: today
abstract: |
  The Census Bureau fields 47 demographic survey instruments containing approximately 7,000 questions, each designed for a specific analytical purpose. No comprehensive map has existed showing where these surveys overlap, where their questions are compatible, and where the differences matter. This research uses AI-assisted methods --- multiple models from competing vendors independently rating question pairs with structured arbitration for disagreements --- to build that map at scale. Across two major survey pairs (CPS and FoodAPS, each scored against ACS), 275 unique source questions shared enough topical ground with ACS to be compared, and approximately 52% of those have at least one viable harmonization path: roughly 19% are directly interchangeable through simple recoding, roughly 33% are linkable with documented statistical adjustments, and roughly 48% measure fundamentally different constructs. Measured against each full instrument, questions with a harmonization path represent about 41% of CPS and 12% of FoodAPS. Among the questions that had ACS territory to be compared against, the rate at which a harmonization path is found is similar for both surveys, 54.8% for CPS and 47.5% for FoodAPS, suggesting the rate reflects shared conceptual territory rather than a survey-specific artifact. The complete analysis was conducted in weeks at a total API cost under \$100. The full pipeline, data, and code are public and reproducible.

  **DRAFT** --- These results are preliminary and have not been independently validated or peer reviewed. Full methodology, data, and code: [github.com/brockwebb/federal-survey-concept-mapper](https://github.com/brockwebb/federal-survey-concept-mapper). The views expressed are the author's own and do not necessarily represent the views of the U.S. Census Bureau or the U.S. Department of Commerce.
